subject: Consolidated Assurance Index (SIG-lite) — delivery windows & custodian mapping
content:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@northbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2029 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidated Assurance Index (SIG-lite) — delivery windows & custodian mapping

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the RFP packet. To make the assurance intake as efficient as possible for both teams, attached is a SIG-lite "Assurance Index" template we use as a first-pass index (assurance-index-template.xlsx).

High-level ask: please populate the template with the artifacts you have available, indicate any custodian/contact for each artifact, and flag any controls where a redaction or alternative substantiation is required. If you can return a filled index, we will:
- map each control to Redwood’s control evidence (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / SIG)
- surface any gaps we recommend addressing immediately (short-term mitigations)
- deliver a consolidated packet for procurement and auditors that includes samples and redaction guidance

Target windows:
- Filled index from NorthBridge: within 4 business days of receipt (we can be flexible)
- Initial mapping & gap summary from Redwood: within 3 business days after we receive the index
- Walkthrough (30–45 min) to review mapping & open questions: schedule on receipt of our mapping

Requested artifacts (examples):
- SOC 2 report (or bridge letter) + List of in-scope services
- ISO 27001 scope and latest certificate (pdf)
- Sample KMS key proof (e.g., key metadata export)
- SIEM/retention policy excerpts and a sample event export (redacted)
- Third-party attestation lists (subprocessors) and any subservice provider contracts if available

We try to avoid sending large bundles initially — the filled index lets us request a minimal representative set. I put a sample KMS proof PDF placeholder in the attachments to show format.

Links: we can accept uploads via the Drive folder (link below) or a secure SFTP if you prefer. We also included a DocuSign onboarding link if your procurement team requires exec-level acceptance before evidence exchange.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleDriveLink
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=EXAMPLE

If helpful, we can run a short index fill workshop (20 min) with your security or procurement team — propose times and we’ll lock one in.

Best,

Rafael Mendes
Senior Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
rafel.mendes@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@northbridge.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@northbridge.com>, Mike Torres <mike.torres@northbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2029 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidated Assurance Index (SIG-lite) — delivery windows & custodian mapping

Hi Rafael,

Thanks — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications before we fill the template: 
1) For KMS proof: do you accept a HSM/KMS metadata export (key IDs, creation timestamps, policy tags) and a short narrative about key rotation practices?
2) For SIEM samples: what time window and anonymization level do you want for the event sample? We need to ensure we keep PII out of the sample.
3) Our procurement team asked whether Redwood will accept encrypted evidence bundles (PGP) in the Drive folder — is that supported?

We can have our security analyst fill the index, but procurement wants to see a high-level delivery schedule for legal review. Mike from procurement (cc’d) will coordinate DocuSign if needed.

Proposed times for a workshop: Tue 23 Jul 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 24 Jul 09:00–09:45 PT. Which works for your team?

Regards,

Sarah Lim
Security Manager, Third-Party Risk
NorthBridge Bank
Sarah.Lim@northbridge.com | +1 (617) 555-0987

---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@northbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement Team <procure@northbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidated Assurance Index (SIG-lite) — delivery windows & custodian mapping

Hi Sarah — great questions. Answers inline: 

1) KMS proof: yes, a metadata export with key IDs, creation/rotation timestamps, KMS policy tags is perfect. We use the metadata primarily to corroborate rotation cadence and separation of duties. The PDF sample (sample-kms-key-proof.pdf) attached in this thread shows the fields we reference. PGP is fine for encrypting the bundle to Drive; we also accept AES-encrypted zip with a separate key share via secure channel.

2) SIEM sample: a 24-hour window is ideal but we can take a shorter window (e.g., 2 hours) for an initial sample. Please redact usernames and IPs if they are sensitive. A short narrative about retention policy and log pipeline (where logs are stored and how long retained) is helpful.

3) Encrypted uploads: confirmed — PGP- or AES-encrypted bundles are supported. If you use PGP, please use our public key (I'll send separately) and add a metadata file that lists filenames and checksums.

Workshop: Tue 23 Jul 10:00 PT works for Kimberly and me — Jordan will cover for follow-ups if anything goes long. I’ll send a calendar invite.

Mapping expectations: once we have the filled index we will produce a mapping table indicating:
- Redwood control ID / description
- Corresponding NorthBridge artifact(s) (filename + custodian)
- Evidence sufficiency (accept / needs redaction / substitution recommended)
- Recommended mitigation or compensating control (if not sufficient)

If you prefer, we can include the procurement team in the mapping review session (short 15 min slot) to accelerate legal sign-off.

Thanks — Rafael
